papers.title: Attack-Resilient Image Watermarking Using Stable Diffusion
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37
limitations: Targeted method/evaluation reading on pp. 1-8; not a complete paper/proof audit.
Local checksum identifies observer notes, not remote PDF bytes.
No reported experiment or code execution was independently reproduced.

evidence.claim: ZoDiac starts from an existing image and optimizes a watermarked diffusion latent with a reconstruction objective.
limitations: Method described by the authors; not independently reproduced.

evidence.claim: The ZoDiac detector uses DDIM inversion, latent Fourier transformation and a statistical test rather than image-domain DCT extraction.
limitations: This describes the paper method, not the precise behavior of the published code.

evidence.claim: The authors evaluate 500 sampled images each from MS-COCO, DiffusionDB and WikiArt.
limitations: Dataset version and image identities were not verified here.

evidence.claim: Existing-image latent embedding and two-domain real/generated evaluation cannot individually be claimed as unique to the thesis candidate because ZoDiac already describes both.
limitations: This narrows two novelty claims; it does not establish or refute originality of the exact dual-signature image-DCT combination.
assumptions: The approved candidate uses an existing-image diffusion/noise route and both photo/generated domains as specified in research/method-spec.md.
No performance number from ZoDiac is treated as a reproduced result or a thesis acceptance threshold.
open_questions: Is an image-domain DCT verifier for the exact joint public OwnerID-bound semantic and perceptual signature combination already described in another inspected prior work?
Can a licensed and checkpoint-pinned ZoDiac/SEAL-class inversion comparator be run under a matched existing-image protocol without changing detector access?
